open_points.subject: randomly minted record identities
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns the randomness source, minting, and collision retry for these identifiers?
options: `store` mints them atomically while checking uniqueness
Each record-owning module mints its own identifiers and asks `store` to reject collisions
A separate lower-level randomness/identity provider owns minting
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` mint and collision-check each random identifier atomically.

open_points.subject: operation-element state needed by run advancement
open_points.text: `runs` reads ... an operation element's conclusion (A11 rule 3) through `effects.operation_element_conclusion`.
open_points.question: What authoritative information does `operation_element_conclusion` return so that `runs` can recover and advance downstream nodes—only the abstract conclusion, or also waiting reason, latest attempt state, and output value/file references?
options: Return the conclusion together with waiting state and immutable output references
Add separate `effects` read capabilities for conclusion, waiting state, and outputs
Allow `runs` to read operation NodeExecution and EffectAttempt records directly from `store`
open_points.default_guess: Return one effects-owned projection containing the conclusion, waiting state, and output references needed by `runs`.

open_points.subject: approval and resolution target association
open_points.text: Whether the run has ended is checked first by `runs`, which owns the run's status; whether the approval is `requested` or the attempt `unknown` is then checked by `effects`, which owns those records.
open_points.question: How does `runs` authoritatively discover which run an `approval_id` or EffectAttempt belongs to before checking that run's status, without reading raw `effects` records?
options: `effects` exposes a read-only target lookup before either decision is written
The request supplies `run_id`, and `effects` validates that the approval or attempt belongs to it
`surface` reads the raw record and supplies its run to `runs`
open_points.default_guess: Require a run identifier in the request and have `effects` validate the association before mutating its record.

open_points.subject: captured trial-case provenance and inputs
open_points.text: `runs` passes to `functions.add_captured_trial_case` the pinned contract version and the inputs of the record it captures ...; `functions` checks that the record's pinned contract version is the one named
open_points.question: What trusted object lets `functions` verify the NodeExecution's provenance, executed implementation, contract version, captured inputs, and `captured_from` identity when `functions` may not know `runs` or `effects` and may not decide from their raw records?
options: `runs` performs all NodeExecution provenance checks and passes a typed, trusted capture package
`store` exposes an atomic capture projection that `functions` may validate
Move construction and provenance validation of the TrialCase to `runs`
open_points.default_guess: Have `runs` pass a typed capture package containing the execution identity, executed implementation, pinned contract version, and exact input references; `functions` validates only contract fit and fixture limits.

open_points.subject: pre-send instance-check sequence
open_points.text: `service_invoker.prepare_request` ... owns every instance failure — no selected instance, no `api_base_url`, a repeated required header, a plain `http` target not allowed ... — resolves the credential through `installation` and places the inputs, in that order
open_points.question: Must `service_invoker` follow this stated sequence, or A09 rule 6's sequence of no instance, missing address, plain HTTP, repeated header, invalid header, unresolved credential, then input placement; and where is `required_header_invalid` checked?
options: Follow A09 rule 6 exactly and treat the State 3 ordering as erroneous
Follow the State 3 ordering and revise A09
Split header validation into `bindings`, changing which module owns the pre-send result
open_points.default_guess: Follow A09 rule 6 exactly, with `service_invoker` checking `required_header_invalid` after repeated headers and before credential resolution.

open_points.subject: spooled effect response interrupted before its NodeExecution
open_points.text: A file spooled before its record is written ... is named by the element's next ordinal ...; start-up recovery uses the EffectAttempt's number too
open_points.question: Who detects and removes or adopts a service-output file that was published to the run spool after a non-read response but before the outcome transaction, when recovery consumes that ordinal by recording the in-flight attempt as `outcome_unknown`?
options: `effects.recover_in_flight_attempts` removes unreferenced files for the recovered attempt
The outcome store call atomically publishes the spool file and records the outcome
`store` scans and removes every unreferenced spool file during start-up recovery
open_points.default_guess: Make publication of a service-output spool file part of the same store operation that records the effect outcome and NodeExecution.

open_points.subject: credential-bearing prepared requests
open_points.text: `service_invoker` owns ... building one HTTP request ... the credential ...; `effects` ... knows `service_invoker` (`prepare` and `send`)
open_points.question: Does `prepare_request` expose the credential-bearing request to `effects`, or return an opaque invoker-owned prepared request plus a separately safe request description; and which module enforces that credential values never enter previews, records, failure details, or logs?
options: Return an opaque prepared-request handle and a credential-free description; `service_invoker` owns secret containment
Return the full request and make `effects` responsible for redaction and non-persistence
Resolve and attach the credential only inside `send_prepared_request` after approval
open_points.default_guess: Keep the credential entirely inside `service_invoker`, exposing only an opaque prepared request and the credential-free request description/digest.
